title: 1 Esdras
lead: 1 Esdras is a Greek book that retells 2 Chronicles 35–36, nearly all of Ezra and part of Nehemiah 8, in a different order and with the added story of Darius's three guards. It is in the Greek Bible and in Orthodox Bibles, in the Apocrypha of many Protestant Bibles, and in an appendix to the Latin Vulgate as 3 Esdras; modern Catholic Bibles leave it out.

sections.b:
The Greek Bible has two books of Esdras. Esdras B (often called 2 Esdras) is a close translation of Ezra–Nehemiah. Esdras A, called 1 Esdras in English, is a freer work. It starts with Josiah's Passover (2 Chronicles 35), runs through the fall of Jerusalem and Cyrus's decree (Ezra 1), moves the Artaxerxes letters of Ezra 4:7–24 to just after Cyrus, and then tells a contest at Darius's court, where young Zerubbabel wins by arguing that women are strongest, and truth strongest of all (1 Esdras 3:1–5:6). Darius rewards him with leave to rebuild. The book ends with Ezra's law reading (Nehemiah 8). Josephus follows it closely in Antiquities 11. Scholars debate whether it is a fragment of an older edition of Ezra or a later reworking; Zipora Talshir argues the second, holding that the story of the three guards is the book's reason for being. Names can confuse: the Latin Vulgate calls it 3 Esdras, and the English Apocrypha's "2 Esdras" is a different book, the apocalypse also called 4 Ezra.

This site cites 1 Esdras in the numbering of Swete's Greek text. The KJV divides chapters 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8 more finely, so its numbers differ there: for example, the list of Cyrus's vessels is 1 Esdras 2:12–13 here and 2:13–14 in the KJV. The 1 Esdras pages show the KJV's number beside each verse.
